_doc: Raids on your base — and the important word is that a raid is a QUEST you take, never an event that happens to you. BUILDING_EXPANSION.md §7.1 and §7.4: a base with no turrets is not raided, because being raided for building a house is a punishment for playing. So the offer needs base size AND defence, both, and js/raid.js will not let a wave spawn until the player has said yes. (§7.20 names Frontier Foundry's wave code as prior art; the shape below is that shape.)
_notorietyDoc: One score out of the things that make a base look worth robbing. Structures and wealth push it up; a waypoint is a beacon and pushes it hard. Notoriety picks which TIER is on offer — it does not start anything.
_gateDoc: BOTH gates, always. `minSize` counts structures; `minDefence` counts turrets, walls, traps and standing guards. A player who builds twenty houses and no wall sees no raid offer at all, which is the point — and a player who wants one sooner builds a turret.
_rewardDoc: §7.13: a rare crate is the FLOOR, never the roll. `crates` lists guaranteed crates by rarity; a tier may add better on top. Materials and blueprints are the pull, standing is the world noticing.

tiers.name: Prowlers at the Fence
tiers.text: Something has been counting your fence posts after dark. Ring the bell and have it out with them.

tiers.name: The Warband
tiers.text: A warband has your smoke on their map. They will come whether you are ready or not — so be ready first.

tiers.name: The Siege
tiers.text: They have brought ladders. Whatever you have built, this is the night it is measured.

tiers.name: The Reckoning
tiers.text: Everything that hates you on this world has agreed on one thing, and the one thing is you.

_nightDoc: §7.18: night raids are harder and pay more. The player chooses when to ring the bell, so this is a real decision rather than a coin toss.
_earlyDoc: §7.4: starting it yourself before the warning runs out is meant to pay. The bonus is on gold only, so it never changes what drops.
_targetDoc: §7.8: raiders walk at ONE thing, so a wall in the right place means something. Preference order — a lit waypoint first (it is the beacon), then the biggest refinery, then the largest store, then the centre of the claim.
_scaleDoc: §7.17: difficulty comes from your level and your defences, never from how many days have passed. A player who spent a week building turrets gets a harder raid because they asked for one.
_lossDoc: §7.11: you can lose, and losing is never a deleted base. Some structures are broken (repairable) and some materials are taken. That is all.
